reviews:
[{'name_person': 'Vimall P Shah', 'time_line': '4 months ago', 'review': "My recent visit to Spin City Kitchen & Bar was an experience of frustrating contrasts, leaving me with mixed feelings that are hard to reconcile.

Let's start with the positive. The atmosphere is undoubtedly appealing; it's a stylish, modern space with a nice vibe that makes a good first impression. This was complemented by genuinely good service. Our server was attentive, friendly, and efficient, ensuring our glasses were never empty and checking in on us at just the right times.

However, these positives were significantly overshadowed by the venue's major drawback: its size. The place is simply too small for the crowd it attracts. Tables are crammed uncomfortably close together, making private conversation nearly impossible and creating a constant, cramped feeling. The noise level was high, and navigating to the restroom felt like an obstacle course.

Unfortunately, the most disappointing aspect was the food, which I found to be below average. While presented nicely, my main course was underseasoned and lacked the freshness and flavour I expected for the price. It felt like a dish going through the motions without any passion or precision.

In conclusion, Spin City has a great foundation with its pleasant atmosphere and excellent staff. But until the significant issues of cramped seating and, most critically, the subpar kitchen offerings are addressed, it's difficult to recommend for anything more than a quick, crowded drink.", 'guided_block': {'GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE': 'Dinner', 'GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE': '₹400–600', 'GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT': 2, 'GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT': 4, 'GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT': 3, 'GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL': 'Not sure', 'GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME': 'No wait', 'GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS': ['Dietary_restrictions', 'E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS', 'Kid-friendliness', 'E:KID_FRIENDLINESS', 'Wheelchair_accessibility', 'E:ACCESSIBILITY']}}, {'name_person': 'Ankeeta', 'time_line': '9 months ago', 'review': "Visited Spin City Kitchen & Bar recently and here’s how the overall experience went. The singer truly added a great energy to the evening!

However, the service left much to be desired. We had to wait for around 45 minutes just to get our starters, and even during that long wait, the mocktails we had ordered didn't arrive. When they did come, the mocktails (Hawai Punch, Virgin Blue Lagoon, and Pink Panther) were quite average — drinkable, but nothing memorable.

Let’s be real—I wanted to love this place. Walking into Malgudi on SV Road, the vibe is immaculate. It sets you up for a cozy, authentic South Indian experience. But between the kitchen confusion and the final bill, it’s a bit of a rollercoaster.
Here is the unfiltered breakdown:
The Star of the Show
If you go here, do yourself a favor and order the Benne Masala Dosa. It was genuinely too good—crispy, buttery, and exactly what you hope for. The chutney pairing was also on point and very tasty.
The "What happened here?" Section
Unfortunately, the rest of the meal felt like an identity crisis.
• The Sambar Situation: This was weird. The sambar actually tasted different across different dishes. Consistency is key, guys—pick a lane!
• Portions & Options: The menu feels very limited, and the portion sizes are basically a tease. For the price, you expect to leave full, not looking for a snack on the way home.
• Overall Taste: Aside from the Benne Dosa, the general taste could really be improved. It feels like they are holding back flavor.
The Coffee Letdown
For a place with this vibe, you expect the coffee game to be strong. It wasn't.
• Coffee Mocktails: Hard pass. They just felt not worth the price tag.
• Filter Coffee: The ultimate test for a South Indian spot, and they failed it. It tasted average at best and definitely lacked that authentic "kick" you crave.
The Final Pinch
Just when you are questioning the portion sizes vs. the price, the bill arrives. They levy a 5% Service Charge.
Paying extra for "service" when the filter coffee is average and the sambar is inconsistent? That stings.
The Verdict
Go for the Benne Masala Dosa and the aesthetic, but lower your expectations for everything else. It’s a great place to sit, but be ready to pay a premium (plus 5%) for a mixed bag of flavors.', 'guided_block': {'GUIDED_DINING_MODE': 'Dine in', 'GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE': 'Brunch', 'GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE': '₹400–600', 'GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT': 3, 'GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT': 4, 'GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT': 4, 'GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME': '10-30 min'}}, {'name_person': 'Dr. Nayan Bheda', 'time_line': '2 months ago', 'review': 'We, a group of six friends, visited Malgudi South Indian Resto-Café, a restaurant owned by celebrated Bollywood personality Shankar Mahadevan.

Unfortunately, the experience did not start on a positive note. Although the restaurant has valet parking, we were denied parking on the grounds that there was no space available. Ironically, we later saw the valet parking other cars—including one of ours—on the street itself. When we decided to park on our own, we easily found enough space on the same street. The valet team did not even attempt to look for parking, which cost us a good 15 minutes and left us puzzled and annoyed.

Once inside, the ambience was a complete contrast—cozy, warm, lively, and very welcoming. The restaurant has a pleasant vibe that makes you want to settle in and enjoy the meal.

The staff was polite and courteous, though service was noticeably slow, possibly due to the crowd.

Food-wise, the experience was mixed. The Medu Vada was a clear disappointment as it was raw from inside, with the taste of uncooked batter evident. The South Khow Suey was a decent attempt, but personally, I still prefer the authentic Burmese-style khow suey.

Among the starters, the Anna Style Crispy Lotus Stem and Butter Pepper Garlic Water Chestnut are worth trying—best enjoyed without high expectations, which actually makes them more enjoyable.

The Mulgabal Dosa is interesting and different, though not extraordinary. It’s enjoyable mainly for the variation. The Truffle Oil Cheese Mushroom Onion Dosa, listed under the “International Dosai Twist” section, did not feel particularly international beyond the name.

The absolute standout of the meal was the Filter Kapi Panna Cotta - easily the best dish we had. It is a must-try and worth ordering even if you are not a coffee lover.

Before leaving, we requested to speak with the chef, who graciously came out to meet us. He is from West Bengal, which was a surprise as we had expected a South Indian chef. When we shared feedback about the vada and a couple of other dishes, he acknowledged the issues immediately - no defensiveness, no excuses. He candidly mentioned that during heavy rush, shortcuts sometimes happen. As a gesture, he offered to treat us to a special sheera, which we politely declined. His honesty and openness genuinely helped make up for the earlier disappointments.

Overall, I’d highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic Indian flavors with a modern twist. I’ll definitely be coming back!

The menu contains pan asian dishes which means everything from sushi, Dimsums, Thai curry to Nasi Goreng, Khao Suey and more is available. Went here for a Sunday lunch and the kitchen service was on time. Thanks to staff Rylan as he made our table service smooth.

APPETISERS~
Volcano Maki Roll -
Fresh prawns with tempura crunch along with veggies tightly rolled with rice topped with spicy sauce tasted delicious. Loved the sushi as it was made perfectly.

Chicken Burnt Garlic Dumpling -
Thin outer covering and nicely filled with minced chicken tasted good. Didn’t felt much of burnt garlic in this however the overall filling tasted good.

Thai Chilli Basil Chicken -

MAINS~

The ambience had a warm, festive vibe that instantly set the mood for a celebratory evening.

Food – Lavish Buffet Spread

The restaurant offered an extensive buffet with an impressive variety in both veg and non-veg sections.

Vegetarian Spread
The veg selection was delightful and flavour-packed. We started with a comforting soup and delicious fried corn, grilled potatoes, and simla mirch starters.
The main course had a wide choice of vegetables and freshly made Indian flatbreads/rotis.
The highlight was the Banjara Special Dal paired with rice, along with traditional Rajasthani khichadi that added an authentic touch.
Desserts were a treat on their own – ghewar, imarti with rabdi, cupcakes, mud cakes, and chocolate mousse, each prepared with great attention to taste and presentation.

Non-Vegetarian Spread
The non-veg section was equally impressive. The chicken soup was perfectly seasoned, and the starters included finely minced mutton and chicken preparations, along with fish, all cooked to perfection.
In the main course, we enjoyed a rich chicken curry, flavourful fish curry, and the standout smoked/dum chicken biryani, which had just the right balance of aroma and spices.

Ambience & Entertainment

To top it all off, the live singer performing 90s Hindi classics created a nostalgic and soothing atmosphere. It elevated the entire dining experience and made our anniversary feel even more special.

We thoroughly enjoyed the food, ambience, and vibe. The combination of authentic Rajasthani décor, a lavish buffet, and soulful live music made it a memorable celebration for us.

One of the major highlights is their dessert selection. The *Death by Chocolate* is a crowd favorite – a decadent, towering mix of chocolate cake, brownie, ice cream, and sauce – not for the faint-hearted or light eaters. It’s rich, heavy, and pure indulgence.

Prices are on the higher side compared to street Chinese joints, but justified by the generous portions and quality of ingredients. Hygiene standards are commendable.

In summary, 5 Spice in Saki Naka lives up to its brand reputation: hearty meals, big servings, flavorful sauces, and comfort food done right. The menu curated by Chef Amninder Sandhu focuses on the philosophy of using open-fire techniques and gas free cooking to bring out natural flavours from the various ingredients and provide a lovely depth to the dishes. She also likes to bring forth dishes which have been forgotten over the years, which really intrigued me to try this spot out in the first place!

Dishes that I tried,
a. Gunpowder Paneer with Manipuri Black Rice Dosa - Rs. 575
-- Super interesting combination which brings forth the lesser known Black rice as an ingredient, creating a crispy yet soft dosa holding a soft paneer packing a punch from the gunpowder. Spicy, soft and yum!

b. Amritsari Kulcha - Rs. 260
-- Nice and crispy with a potato onion filling, it's simple and pairs extremely well with the dal makhani or even great by itself! Would have liked if it was served with something on the side though!

c. Veg Biryani
-- Fills the table with a lovely aroma as soon as it arrives, the rice is fluffy and the use of spices is beautiful especially the saffron! Quantity is really a lot and you should not miss their Biryanis. ✨

d. Bawri Jamun (My personal favorite) - Rs. 575
-- A giant gulab jamun filled with dry fruits and mawa, it's the perfect indulgent end to the meal and the highlight is definitely their Rabdi which is used as a topping - I ended up getting some more on the side by itself 🤍

[{'name_person': 'Serena M', 'time_line': 'a month ago', 'review': 'I had the most beautiful experience at Madeleine de Proust. The decor is absolutely stunning so elegant, refined, and thoughtfully curated. From the moment you walk in, it truly feels like you’ve been transported to a chic Parisian salon. The ambiance is soft, romantic, and effortlessly sophisticated.

I came for afternoon tea, and the presentation was simply exquisite. Every detail was beautifully arranged, and everything tasted incredibly fresh and delicious. The scones were perfect and paired with the most luscious clotted cream (which I absolutely loved). You can really taste the quality in every bite.

The combination of vinegar, sauce, and some burnt garlic and cabbage strips made the whole dish taste amazing. For the mocktails, we went ahead with sweetheart, a combination of pomegranate and pineapple juice with some salt and spice on the glass rim. The pink lemonade was a lemonade mixed with some watermelon juice to make a unique blend. Both tasted delicious. We also ordered the pineapple spritzer, which was juice and soda mixed with some ice. It was refreshing to say.

Next, we ordered pav bhaji tartlets, and this is where the taste went down. Tartlets were small cup-shaped biscuits filled with pav bhaji and topped with cheese. Also, the music was so loud by nighttime that it would have almost ripped off our eardrums. The whole table was vibrating, and it was deafening. We literally had to get the pizza parcel and run from the place. And when the place gets crowded, the service becomes exceptionally sluggish.

[{'name_person': 'sam mahtani', 'time_line': 'a month ago', 'review': 'Mumbai, and especially Bandra West (with another outlet in Churchgate), should be delighted to welcome Mezcalita—a bright and comfortable Mexican cantina/taquería. The service, led by Pinku and his team, is caring, attentive, and genuinely warm, while the food strikes a perfect balance between creativity and authenticity.

The menu is vibrant and visually engaging, guiding guests toward a true Mexican culinary adventure, with comfort food taking center stage.

The Guacamole (GUAC), made with fresh Hass avocados, delivers a creamy texture and rich, buttery flavor. Blended with tomatoes, onions, a dash of lime, and a subtle kick of habanero chilies, it is simply delicious and divine.

I  was especially blown away by the habanero-laced cottage cheese cubes, paired with soy protein and other fresh ingredients. This appetizer is packed with flavor and offers great value for money. Pro tip: always pair it with a glass of Horchata—Mexico’s national drink—made from rice milk, cardamom, cinnamon, and both evaporated and condensed milk.

Mezcalita also shows its sensibility by baking its own bread for the Tortas (Mexican sandwiches). The Telera buns, with their crisp crust and fluffy interior, elevate the experience. The cottage cheese Chilaquiles Torta was an absolute delight.

The black bean vegetarian burritos were impressively well-balanced and just the right size for a single taster portion.

For your next Mexican culinary journey, head to Mezcalita at Pali Hill. Explore their wide range of cocktails, and don’t hesitate to reach out to Pinku, the manager, for a thoughtfully chosen table.

Final note: Mezcalita isn’t just a restaurant—it’s a celebration of Mexican flavors brought to life with care, creativity, and authenticity. [{'name_person': 'J S', 'time_line': '2 weeks ago', 'review': 'The place promises a lot but fails to deliver. Be it the ambience or the food.

They messed up our reservation in their list and it had to be established to them that we held a reservation through district before we were shown to our table.

Also, siting in the compound of a building near the main door of the restuarant on oversized unwieldy chairs is not my idea of a fine dine restaurant.

•	Smoked Avocado – The plating on this was stunning, and the charred flavor was perfect.
•	Bucatini – Who knew pasta could be this bold? The pecorino fondue and chilli crisp gave it an edge we loved.

The Strawberry dessert (the one with crushed berries, crumbles, and pops of basil) was refreshing, vibrant, and light.
But the real heart-stealer? The Brûlée – smooth, rich, and just the right amount of caramelised crunch.

Service:

The staff was warm, well-informed, and knew the menu in and out. Our server Jeremiah ensured everything came out smoothly and timed well.

The attention to detail—both in flavor and presentation—makes Paradox a must-visit. Every dish felt thoughtful and daring. This wasn’t just a meal; it was an experience.
